newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PALM OIL - Southeast Asia markets seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: PALM OIL - Southeast Asia markets seen mixed.

text.p: Asian palm oil markets are likely to be mixed this week, with consumer demand before the Eid al-Fitr holiday, which ends the Moslem fasting month, underpinning Indonesian prices, traders said.
But Malaysian prices may weaken on the back of poor export data while the Singapore market will be range-bound, they said.
"We expect there will be some price movement this week," said an Indonesian trader.
Another trader said: "I expect demand to pick up this week, and prices are likely to edge up slightly."
Indonesian refiners say there was no margin in processing olein because of the relatively high price of crude palm oil.
Indonesian palm olein finished last week in Jakarta at 1,430-35 rupiah/kg, compared with 1,445-50 previously.
In Malaysia, prices are likely to ease.
"Exports look bad in January. We only expect January 1-25 export estimates to be around 410,000 tonnes," a trader said, adding that shipments were slow with no fresh tenders from major buyers.
Cargo surveyor SGS (M) Bhd was expected to release its January 1-25 export data on Monday. SGS put exports for December 1-25 at 589,456 tonnes.
"Prices are relatively high and buyers are staying away and hoping for the market to come down. Business was mainly from hand to mouth," the trader said.

"Prices have been high and a technical correction was much needed," another trader said. Prices would weaken this week despite an expectation of a double-digit decline in the January production because of unfavourable weather conditions in the East Malaysian state of Sabah, he added.
The market has forecast January's output would fall by 10 to 12 percent over December, against crop forecaster Ivan Wong's estimate of a nine percent fall.
Singapore palm oil will remain rangebound with support for the April futures contract on the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange pegged at 1,260 ringgit a tonne.
Most traders attributed the quiet market to the Moslem Ramadan fasting month and the market winding down before the Eid-al-Fitr and Chinese Lunar New Year holidays next month.
Traders in Kuala Lumpur said Malaysia's benchmark April futures, which also closed on Friday at 1,260 ringgit, could fall slightly below 1,250 ringgit this week unless supportive news appears.
"There is nothing too exciting to stir market either way," said a trader in Singapore. "All the bullish news has become stale."

Another Singaporean trader said: "If levels break the 1,260 support, we may see a lot of selling. But levels have recently rebounded with pockets of demand seen -- chances of breaking that support (1,260) may be slim."
(With contributions from K.T. Arasu in Indonesia and Ang Bee Lin in Singapore). ($1 = 2.48 ringgit, $1 = 2,370 rupiah)
